alerts.reason: Revenue growth slowed from 36.84% in March to 23.35% in June (A). Distribution gains support a September result above -5%, but Celsius's largest distributor was already reducing inventory days (C). Further cuts in its orders could push December revenue down at least 5% year over year.

Reported sales fell 3.78% year over year in March and 1.26% in June, supporting a September forecast above -5%. Lower sales and production volumes (E) and weaker aerospace and defense sales in Asia Pacific (A) leave Kennametal exposed to a December decline of at least 5% if volume losses deepen.

Net sales swung from 15.88% growth in March to a 3.55% decline in June (A). Higher Work Truck Solutions volume and pricing could keep September above -5%, but low snowfall had already reduced attachment volumes (C, D). A further 1.45 percentage points of deterioration from June would put December at the threshold.

Reported net sales fell 4.63% in March and 1.77% in June. Contractual pricing partly offset volume cuts at plants undergoing turnarounds (A), supporting a September decline short of 5%. Further plant volume cuts could outweigh that offset and push the December decline to at least 5% (A, D).

June net sales fell just 1.3%, but the order backlog fell 22.9% year over year, from $688.8 million to $531.1 million (A, C). Existing orders could sustain September sales above the threshold, while the smaller backlog leaves fewer orders to ship in December.

June net sales rose 2.9% as improved parts availability let Tennant fill back orders (A, B). Backlog fell from $186.2 million in December to $110.0 million in June (C). Filling remaining orders could support September sales, but by December a smaller backlog and weakness in EMEA and APAC (D) could push consolidated sales down at least 5%.

Cerence accelerated $67.8 million of deferred revenue into fiscal Q1 2024 (C), raising the comparison specifically for the quarter beginning October 2024. June revenue grew 14.4% (A), supporting a September result above -5%. The prior December quarter had roughly $138.4 million of revenue, inferred from B and the March and June figures, so even $131.4 million this December would trigger the crossing.

Schneider's reported revenue decline narrowed from 7.68% in March to 2.21% in June (A), supporting a September result above -5%. Logistics revenue excluding fuel surcharges fell $24.6 million as both revenue per order and brokerage volume declined (B). Deeper losses on both measures could take the consolidated December decline back to at least 5%.
